paragraph.heading: Use of funds.—
paragraph.chapeau: With respect to funds made available under this section for fiscal years 2019 through 2023—

subparagraph.content: for each fiscal year the Secretary shall use not more than 10 percent of such funds available for such fiscal year for the produce prescription program described in subsection (c);

for each fiscal year not more than 8 percent of such funds available for such fiscal year shall be used by the National Institute of Food and Agriculture and the Food and Nutrition Service for administration; and

subparagraph.chapeau: the Secretary shall use for the Nutrition Incentive Program Training, Technical Assistance, Evaluation, and Information Centers established under subsection (e) not more than—

clause.content: $17,000,000 in the aggregate for fiscal years 2019 and 2020; and
$7,000,000 for each of the fiscal years 2021 through 2023.

section.heading: EFFECTIVE AND IMPLEMENTATION DATES.
section.content: Except as otherwise provided in this title, this title and the amendments made by this title take effect on October 1, 2008.

subsection.chapeau: Except as otherwise provided in this subtitle, in this subtitle:

paragraph.heading: Capacity and infrastructure program.—
paragraph.content: The term “capacity and infrastructure program” has the meaning given the term in subsection (f)(1) of section 251 of the Department of Agriculture Reorganization Act of 1994 (7 U.S.C. 6971) (as added by section 7511(a)(4)).

paragraph.heading: Capacity and infrastructure program critical base funding.—
paragraph.content: The term “capacity and infrastructure program critical base funding” means the aggregate amount of Federal funds made available for capacity and infrastructure programs for fiscal year 2006, as appropriate.

paragraph.heading: Competitive program.—
paragraph.content: The term “competitive program” has the meaning given the term in subsection (f)(1) of section 251 of the Department of Agriculture Reorganization Act of 1994 (7 U.S.C. 6971) (as added by section 7511(a)(4)).

paragraph.heading: Competitive program critical base funding.—
paragraph.content: The term “competitive program critical base funding” means the aggregate amount of Federal funds made available for competitive programs for fiscal year 2006, as appropriate.

paragraph.heading: Hispanic-serving agricultural colleges and universities.—
paragraph.content: The term “Hispanic-serving agricultural colleges and universities” has the meaning given the term in section 1404 of the National Agricultural Research, Extension, and Teaching Policy Act of 1977 (7 U.S.C. 3103).

paragraph.heading: NLGCA institution.—
paragraph.content: The term “NLGCA Institution” has the meaning given the term in section 1404 of the National Agricultural Research, Extension, and Teaching Policy Act of 1977 (7 U.S.C. 3103).

paragraph.heading: 1862 institution; 1890 institution; 1994 institution.—
paragraph.content: The terms “1862 Institution”, “1890 Institution”, and “1994 Institution” have the meanings given the terms in section 2 of the Agricultural Research, Extension, and Education Reform Act of 1998 (7 U.S.C. 7601).

section.heading: GRAZINGLANDS RESEARCH LABORATORY.
section.content: Except as otherwise specifically authorized by law and notwithstanding any other provision of law, the Federal land and facilities at El Reno, Oklahoma, administered by the Secretary (as of the date of enactment of this Act) as the Grazinglands Research Laboratory, shall not at any time, in whole or in part, be declared to be excess or surplus Federal property under chapter 5 of subtitle I of title 40, United States Code, or otherwise be conveyed or transferred in whole or in part, for the period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act and ending on September 30, 2026.

section.heading: FORT RENO SCIENCE PARK RESEARCH FACILITY.
section.content: The Secretary may lease land to the University of Oklahoma at the Grazinglands Research Laboratory at El Reno, Oklahoma, on such terms and conditions as the University and the Secretary may agree in furtherance of cooperative research and existing easement arrangements.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary, acting through the Under Secretary of Research, Education, and Economics (referred to in this section as the “Under Secretary”), shall commence preparation of a roadmap for agricultural research, education, and extension that—

paragraph.content: identifies current trends and constraints;
identifies major opportunities and gaps that no single entity within the Department of Agriculture would be able to address individually;

paragraph.chapeau: involves—

subparagraph.content: interested parties from the Federal Government and nongovernmental entities; and

the National Agricultural Research, Extension, Education, and Economics Advisory Board established under section 1408 of the National Agricultural Research, Extension, and Teaching Policy Act of 1977 (7 U.S.C. 3123);

paragraph.content: incorporates roadmaps for agricultural research, education, and extension made publicly available by other Federal entities, agencies, or offices; and

paragraph.chapeau: describes recommended funding levels for areas of agricultural research, education, and extension, including—

subparagraph.content: competitive programs;

subparagraph.chapeau: capacity and infrastructure programs, with attention to the future growth needs of—

clause.content: small 1862 Institutions, 1890 Institutions, and 1994 Institutions;
Hispanic-serving agricultural colleges and universities;
NLGCA Institutions; and
colleges of veterinary medicine; and

subparagraph.content: intramural programs at agencies within the research, education, and economics mission area; and

paragraph.content: describes how organizational changes enacted by this Act have impacted agricultural research, extension, and education across the Department of Agriculture, including minimization of unnecessary programmatic and administrative duplication.

subsection.heading: Reviewability.—
subsection.content: The roadmap described in this section shall not be subject to review by any officer or employee of the Federal Government other than the Secretary (or a designee of the Secretary).

subsection.heading: Roadmap Implementation and Report.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 1 year after the date on which the Secretary commences preparation of the roadmap under this section, the Secretary shall—

paragraph.content: implement and use the roadmap to set the research, education, and extension agenda of the Department of Agriculture; and
make the roadmap available to the public.

section.heading: REVIEW OF PLAN OF WORK REQUIREMENTS.

subsection.heading: Review.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall work with university partners in extension and research to review and identify measures to streamline the submission, reporting under, and implementation of plan of work requirements, including those requirements under—

paragraph.content: sections 1444(d) and 1445(c) of the National Agricultural Research, Extension, and Teaching Policy Act of 1977 (7 U.S.C. 3221(d) and 3222(c), respectively);
section 7 of the Hatch Act of 1887 (7 U.S.C. 361g); and
section 4 of the Smith-Lever Act (7 U.S.C. 344).

subsection.heading: Consultation.—
subsection.content: In carrying out the review and formulating and compiling the recommendations, the Secretary shall consult with the land-grant institutions.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Covered program.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “covered program” means—

subparagraph.content: each research program carried out by the Agricultural Research Service or the Economic Research Service for which annual appropriations are requested in the annual budget submission of the President; and
each competitive program carried out by the National Institute of Food and Agriculture for which annual appropriations are requested in the annual budget submission of the President.

paragraph.heading: Request for applications.—
paragraph.content: The term “request for applications” means a funding announcement published by the National Institute of Food and Agriculture that provides detailed information on funding opportunities at the Institute, including the purpose, eligibility, restriction, focus areas, evaluation criteria, regulatory information, and instructions on how to apply for such opportunities.

subsection.heading: Budget Request.—
subsection.content: The President shall submit to Congress, together with the annual budget submission of the President, a single budget line item reflecting the total amount requested by the President for funding for research, education, and extension activities of the Research, Education, and Economics mission area of the Department for that fiscal year and for the preceding 5 fiscal years.

subsection.heading: Capacity and Infrastructure Program Request.—
subsection.chapeau: Of the funds requested for capacity and infrastructure programs in excess of the capacity and infrastructure program critical base funding level, budgetary emphasis should be placed on enhancing funding for—

paragraph.content: 1890 Institutions;
1994 Institutions;
NLGCA Institutions;
Hispanic-serving agricultural colleges and universities; and
small 1862 Institutions.

subsection.heading: Competitive Program Request.—
subsection.chapeau: Of the funds requested for competitive programs in excess of the competitive program critical base funding level, budgetary emphasis should be placed on—

paragraph.content: enhancing funding for emerging problems; and
finding solutions for those problems.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: Each year, the President shall submit to Congress for each funding request for a covered program—

subparagraph.content: in the case of the information described in paragraph (2), such information together with the annual budget submission of the President; and

in the case of any additional information described in paragraph (3), such additional information within a reasonable period that begins after the date of the annual budget submission of the President.

paragraph.heading: Information described.—
paragraph.chapeau: The information described in this paragraph includes—

subparagraph.chapeau: baseline information, including with respect to each covered program—

clause.content: the funding level for the program for the fiscal year preceding the year for which the annual budget submission of the President is submitted;
the funding level requested in the annual budget submission of the President, including any increase or decrease in the funding level; and
an explanation justifying any change from the funding level specified in clause (i) to the level specified in clause (ii);

subparagraph.content: with respect to each covered program that is carried out by the Economic Research Service or the Agricultural Research Service, the location and staff years of the program;

subparagraph.chapeau: the proposed funding levels to be allocated to, and the expected publication date, scope, and allocation level for, each request for applications to be published under or associated with—

clause.content: each grant and cooperative agreement awarded under subsection (d) of section 2501 of the Food, Agriculture, Conservation, and Trade Act of 1990 (7 U.S.C. 2279);
each priority area specified in subsection (b)(2) of the Competitive, Special, and Facilities Research Grant Act (7 U.S.C. 3157(b)(2));
each research and extension project carried out under section 1621(a) of the Food, Agriculture, Conservation, and Trade Act of 1990 (7 U.S.C. 5811(a));
each grant awarded under section 1672B(a) of the Food, Agriculture, Conservation, and Trade Act of 1990 (7 U.S.C. 5925b(a)); and
each grant awarded under section 412(d) of the Agricultural Research, Extension, and Education Reform Act of 1998 (7 U.S.C. 7632(d)); and

subparagraph.content: any other information the Secretary determines will increase congressional oversight with respect to covered programs.

paragraph.heading: Additional information described.—
paragraph.content: The additional information described in this paragraph is information that the Secretary, after consulting with the Committee on Agriculture of the House of Representatives, the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry of the Senate, and the Subcommittees on Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies of the Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate, determines is a necessary revision or clarification to the information described in paragraph (2).

paragraph.heading: Prohibition.—
paragraph.chapeau: Unless the President submits the information described in paragraph (2)(C) for a fiscal year, the President may not carry out any program during that fiscal year that is authorized under—

subparagraph.content: subsection (d) of section 2501 of the Food, Agriculture, Conservation, and Trade Act of 1990 (7 U.S.C. 2279);
subsection (b) of the Competitive, Special, and Facilities Research Grant Act (7 U.S.C. 3157(b));
section 1621 of the Food, Agriculture, Conservation, and Trade Act of 1990 (7 U.S.C. 5811);
section 1672B of the Food, Agriculture, Conservation, and Trade Act of 1990 (7 U.S.C. 5925b); or
section 412 of the Agricultural Research, Extension, and Education Reform Act of 1998 (7 U.S.C. 7632).

subsection.heading: Report of the Secretary of Agriculture.—
subsection.chapeau: Each year on a date that is not later than the date on which the President submits the annual budget, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report containing a description of the agricultural research, extension, and education activities carried out by the Federal Government during the fiscal year that immediately precedes the year for which the report is submitted, including—

paragraph.chapeau: a review of the extent to which those activities—

subparagraph.content: are duplicative or overlap within the Department of Agriculture; or

subparagraph.chapeau: are similar to activities carried out by—

clause.content: other Federal agencies;
the States (including the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico and other territories or possessions of the United States);
institutions of higher education (as defined in section 101 of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (20 U.S.C. 1001)); or
the private sector; and

paragraph.content: for each report submitted under this section on or after January 1, 2014, a 5-year projection of national priorities with respect to agricultural research, extension, and education, taking into account domestic needs.

subsection.heading: Interchangeability of Funds.—
subsection.content: Nothing in this section shall be construed so as to limit the authority of the Secretary under section 702(b) of the Department of Agriculture Organic Act of 1944 (7 U.S.C. 2257(b)), with respect to the reprogramming or transfer of funds.

section.heading: RESEARCH AND EDUCATION GRANTS FOR THE STUDY OF ANTIBIOTIC-RESISTANT BACTERIA.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall provide research and education grants, on a competitive basis—

paragraph.chapeau: to study the development of antibiotic-resistant bacteria, including—

subparagraph.content: movement of antibiotic-resistant bacteria into groundwater and surface water; and
the effect on antibiotic resistance from various drug use regimens; and

paragraph.chapeau: to study and ensure the judicious use of antibiotics in veterinary and human medicine, including—

subparagraph.content: methods and practices of animal husbandry;
safe and effective alternatives to antibiotics;
the development of better veterinary diagnostics to improve decisionmaking; and
the identification of conditions or factors that affect antibiotic use on farms.

subsection.heading: Administration.—
subsection.content: Paragraphs (4), (7), (8), and (11)(B) of subsection (b) of the Competitive, Special, and Facilities Research Grant Act (7 U.S.C. 450i) shall apply with respect to the making of grants under this section.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There are authorized to be appropriated such sums as are necessary to carry out this section for each of fiscal years 2008 through 2012.

section.heading: FARM AND RANCH STRESS ASSISTANCE NETWORK.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary, in coordination with the Secretary of Health and Human Services, shall make competitive grants to eligible entities described in subsection (c) to establish a Farm and Ranch Stress Assistance Network that provides stress assistance programs to individuals who are engaged in farming, ranching, and other agriculture-related occupations.

subsection.heading: Eligible Programs.—
subsection.chapeau: Grants awarded under subsection (a) may be used—

paragraph.chapeau: to initiate, expand, or sustain programs that provide professional agricultural behavioral health counseling and referral for other forms of assistance as necessary through—

subparagraph.content: farm telephone helplines and websites;

subparagraph.chapeau: training, including training programs and workshops, for—

clause.content: advocates for individuals who are engaged in farming, ranching, and other occupations relating to agriculture; and

clause.chapeau: other individuals and entities that may assist individuals who—

subclause.content: are engaged in farming, ranching, and other occupations relating to agriculture; and
are in crisis;

subparagraph.content: support groups; and
outreach services and activities, including the dissemination of information and materials; or

paragraph.content: to enter into contracts, on a multiyear basis, with community-based, direct-service organizations to initiate, expand, or sustain programs described in paragraph (1) and subsection (a).

subsection.heading: Eligible Recipients.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary may award a grant under this section to—

paragraph.content: an Indian tribe (as defined in section 4 of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act (25 U.S.C. 5304));
a State department of agriculture;
a State cooperative extension service;
a qualified nonprofit organization, as determined by the Secretary;
an entity providing appropriate services, as determined by the Secretary, in 1 or more States; or
a partnership carried out by 2 or more entities described in paragraphs (1) through (5).

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out this section $10,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2019 through 2023.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this subsection, the Secretary, in coordination with the Secretary of Health and Human Services, shall submit to Congress and any other relevant Federal department or agency, and make publicly available, a report describing the state of behavioral and mental health of individuals who are engaged in farming, ranching, and other occupations relating to agriculture.

paragraph.heading: Contents.—
paragraph.chapeau: The report under paragraph (1) shall include—

subparagraph.chapeau: an inventory and assessment of efforts to support the behavioral and mental health of individuals who are engaged in farming, ranching, and other occupations relating to agriculture by—

clause.content: the Federal Government, States, and units of local government;
communities comprised of those individuals;
health care providers;
State cooperative extension services; and
other appropriate entities, as determined by the Secretary;

subparagraph.content: a description of the challenges faced by individuals who are engaged in farming, ranching, and other occupations relating to agriculture that may impact the behavioral and mental health of farmers and ranchers;

a description of how the Department of Agriculture can improve coordination and cooperation with Federal health departments and agencies, including the Department of Health and Human Services, the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration, the Health Resources and Services Administration, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and the National Institutes of Health, to best address the behavioral and mental health of individuals who are engaged in farming, ranching, and other occupations relating to agriculture;

a long-term strategy for responding to the challenges described under subparagraph (B) and recommendations based on best practices for further action to be carried out by appropriate Federal departments or agencies to improve Federal Government response and seek to prevent suicide among individuals who are engaged in farming, ranching, and other occupations relating to agriculture; and

subparagraph.chapeau: an evaluation of the impact that behavioral and mental health challenges and outcomes (including suicide) among individuals who are engaged in farming, ranching, and other agriculture related occupations have on—

clause.content: the agricultural workforce;
agricultural production;
rural families and communities; and
succession planning.

subsection.heading: State Defined.—
subsection.content: For purposes of this section, the term “State” has the meaning given such term in section 1404 of the National Agricultural Research, Extension, and Teaching Policy Act of 1977 (7 U.S.C. 3103).

section.heading: LIVE VIRUS FOOT AND MOUTH DISEASE RESEARCH.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall issue a permit required under section 12 of the Act of May 29, 1884 (21 U.S.C. 113a) to the Secretary of Homeland Security for work on the live virus of foot and mouth disease at any facility that is a successor to the Plum Island Animal Disease Center and charged with researching high-consequence biological threats involving zoonotic and foreign animal diseases (referred to in this section as the “successor facility”).

subsection.heading: Limitation to Single Facility.—
subsection.content: Not more than 1 facility shall be issued a permit under subsection (a).

subsection.heading: Limitation on Validity.—
subsection.content: The permit issued under this section shall be valid unless the Secretary determines that the study of live foot and mouth disease virus at the successor facility is not being carried out in accordance with the regulations promulgated by the Secretary pursuant to the Agricultural Bioterrorism Protection Act of 2002 (7 U.S.C. 8401 et seq.).

subsection.heading: Authority.—
subsection.chapeau: The suspension, revocation, or other impairment of the permit issued under this section—

paragraph.content: shall be made by the Secretary; and
is a nondelegable function.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall establish within the Department a natural products research program.

subsection.heading: Duties.—
subsection.chapeau: In carrying out the program established under subsection (a), the Secretary shall coordinate research relating to natural products, including—

paragraph.content: research to improve human health and agricultural productivity through the discovery, development, and commercialization of products and agrichemicals from bioactive natural products, including products from plant, marine, and microbial sources;
research to characterize the botanical sources, production, chemistry, and biological properties of plant-derived natural products; and
other research priorities identified by the Secretary.

subsection.heading: Peer and Merit Review.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall—

paragraph.content: determine the relevance and merit of research under this section through a system of peer review established by the Secretary pursuant to section 103 of the Agricultural Research, Extension, and Education Reform Act of 1998 (7 U.S.C. 7613); and
approve funding for research on the basis of merit, quality, and relevance to advancing the purposes of this section.

subsection.heading: Buildings and Facilities.—
subsection.content: Funds made available under this section shall not be used for the construction of a new building or facility or the acquisition, expansion, remodeling, or alteration of an existing building or facility (including site grading and improvement and architect fees).

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There are authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $7,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2014 through 2023.

subsection.heading: Establishment.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall establish and carry out a program to provide grants to the sun grant centers and subcenter specified in subsection (b)—

paragraph.content: to enhance national energy security through the development, distribution, and implementation of biobased energy technologies;
to promote diversification in, and the environmental sustainability of, agricultural production in the United States through biobased energy and product technologies;
to promote economic diversification in rural areas of the United States through biobased energy and product technologies; and

paragraph.chapeau: to enhance the efficiency of bioenergy and biomass research and development programs through improved coordination and collaboration among—

subparagraph.content: the Department of Agriculture;
other appropriate Federal agencies (as determined by the Secretary); and
land-grant colleges and universities.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall use amounts made available under subsection (g) to provide grants to each of the following:

subparagraph.heading: North-central center.—
subparagraph.content: A north-central sun grant center for the region composed of the States of Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Minnesota, Montana, Nebraska, North Dakota, South Dakota, Wisconsin, and Wyoming.

subparagraph.heading: Southeastern center.—
subparagraph.chapeau: A southeastern sun grant center for the region composed of—

clause.content: the States of Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, and Virginia;
the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico; and
the United States Virgin Islands.

subparagraph.heading: South-central center.—
subparagraph.content: A south-central sun grant center for the region composed of the States of Arkansas, Colorado, Kansas, Louisiana, Missouri, New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Texas.

subparagraph.heading: Western center.—
subparagraph.chapeau: A western sun grant center for the region composed of—

clause.content: the States of Alaska, Arizona, California, Hawaii, Idaho, Nevada, Oregon, Utah, and Washington; and

insular areas (as defined in section 1404 of the National Agricultural Research, Extension, and Teaching Policy Act of 1977 (7 U.S.C. 3103 (other than the insular areas referred to in clauses (ii) and (iii) of subparagraph (B))).

subparagraph.heading: Northeastern center.—
subparagraph.content: A northeastern sun grant center for the region composed of the States of Connecticut, Delaware, Massachusetts, Maryland, Maine, Michigan, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Vermont, and West Virginia.

subparagraph.heading: Western insular pacific subcenter.—
subparagraph.content: A western insular Pacific sun grant subcenter for the region of Alaska, Hawaii, Guam, American Samoa, the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, the Federated States of Micronesia, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, and the Republic of Palau.

subparagraph.heading: Centers.—
subparagraph.content: In providing any funds made available under subsection (g), the Secretary shall distribute the grants in equal amounts to the sun grant centers described in subparagraphs (A) through (E) of paragraph (1).

subparagraph.heading: Subcenter.—
subparagraph.content: The sun grant center described in paragraph (1)(D) shall allocate a portion of the funds received under paragraph (1) to the subcenter described in paragraph (1)(F) pursuant to guidance issued by the Secretary.

paragraph.heading: Failure to comply with requirements.—
paragraph.content: If the Secretary finds on the basis of a review of the annual report required under subsection (f) or on the basis of an audit of a sun grant center or subcenter conducted by the Secretary that the center or subcenter has not complied with the requirements of this section, the sun grant center or subcenter shall be ineligible to receive further grants under this section for such period of time as may be prescribed by the Secretary.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: A sun grant center or subcenter shall use 75 percent of the funds described in subsection (b) to provide competitive grants to entities that are—

clause.content: eligible to receive grants under subsection (b)(7) of the Competitive, Special, and Facilities Research Grant Act (7 U.S.C. 450i(b)(7)); and
located in the region covered by the sun grant center or subcenter.

subparagraph.heading: Activities.—
subparagraph.content: Grants described in subparagraph (A) shall be used by the grant recipient to conduct, in a manner consistent with the purposes described in subsection (a), multi-institutional and integrated, multistate research, extension, and education programs on technology development and technology implementation.

clause.heading: Peer and merit review.—
clause.chapeau: In making grants under this paragraph, a sun grant center or subcenter shall—

subclause.content: seek and accept proposals for grants;

determine the relevance and merit of proposals through a system of peer review similar to that established by the Secretary pursuant to section 103 of the Agricultural Research, Extension, and Education Reform Act of 1998 (7 U.S.C. 7613); and
award grants on the basis of merit, quality, and relevance to advancing the purposes of this section.

clause.heading: Priority.—
clause.content: A sun grant center or subcenter shall give a higher priority to programs that are consistent with the plan approved by the Secretary under subsection (d).

clause.heading: Term.—
clause.content: A grant awarded by a sun grant center or subcenter shall have a term that does not exceed 5 years.

subclause.heading: In general.—
subclause.content: Except as provided in subclauses (II) and (III), as a condition of receiving a grant under this paragraph, the sun grant center or subcenter shall require that not less than 20 percent of the cost of an activity described in subparagraph (B) be matched with funds, including in-kind contributions, from a non-Federal source.

subclause.heading: Exclusion.—
subclause.content: Subclause (I) shall not apply to fundamental research (as defined in subsection (f)(1) of section 251 of the Department of Agriculture Reorganization Act of 1994 (7 U.S.C. 6971) (as added by section 7511(a)(4)).

subclause.heading: Reduction.—
subclause.content: The sun grant center or subcenter may reduce or eliminate the requirement for non-Federal funds under subclause (I) for applied research (as defined in subsection (f)(1) of section 251 of the Department of Agriculture Reorganization Act of 1994 (7 U.S.C. 6971) (as added by section 7511(a)(4)) if the sun grant center or subcenter determines that the reduction is necessary and appropriate pursuant to guidance issued by the Secretary.

clause.heading: Buildings and facilities.—
clause.content: Funds made available for grants shall not be used for the construction of a new building or facility or the acquisition, expansion, remodeling, or alteration of an existing building or facility (including site grading and improvement and architect fees).

clause.heading: Limitation on indirect costs.—
clause.content: A sun grant center or subcenter may not recover the indirect costs of making grants under subparagraph (A).

paragraph.heading: Administrative expenses.—
paragraph.content: A sun grant center or subcenter may use up to 4 percent of the funds described in subsection (b) to pay administrative expenses incurred in carrying out paragraph (1).

paragraph.heading: Research, extension and educational activities.—
paragraph.chapeau: The sun grant centers and subcenter shall use the remainder of the funds described in subsection (b) to conduct, in a manner consistent with the purposes described in subsection (a), multi-institutional and multistate—

subparagraph.content: research, extension, and educational programs on technology development; and
integrated research, extension, and educational programs on technology implementation.

subsection.heading: Plan for Research Activities to Be Funded.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Subject to the availability of funds under subsection (g), and in cooperation with land-grant colleges and universities and private industry , the sun grant centers and subcenter shall jointly develop and submit to the Secretary for approval a plan for addressing the bioenergy, biomass, and bioproducts research priorities of the Department of Agriculture and other appropriate Federal agencies at the State and regional levels.

paragraph.heading: Funding.—
paragraph.content: Funds described in subsection (c)(2) shall be available to carry out planning coordination under paragraph (1).

paragraph.heading: Use of plan.—
paragraph.content: The sun grant centers and subcenter shall use the plan described in paragraph (1) in making grants under subsection (c)(1).

subsection.heading: Grant Information Analysis Center.—
subsection.content: The sun grant centers and subcenter shall maintain a Sun Grant Information Analysis Center at the sun grant center specified in subsection (b)(1)(A) to provide the sun grant centers and subcenter with analysis and data management support.

subsection.heading: Annual Reports.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 90 days after the end of each fiscal year, a sun grant center or subcenter receiving a grant under this section shall submit to the Secretary a report that describes the policies, priorities, and operations of the program carried out by the center or subcenter during the fiscal year, including—

paragraph.content: the results of all peer and merit review procedures conducted pursuant to subsection (c)(1)(C)(i); and
a description of progress made in facilitating the priorities described in subsection (d)(1).

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $75,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2008 through 2023, of which not more than $4,000,000 for each fiscal year shall be made available to carry out subsection (e).

section.heading: DEMONSTRATION PROJECT AUTHORITY FOR TEMPORARY POSITIONS.
section.content: Notwithstanding section 4703(d)(1) of title 5, United States Code, the amendment to the personnel management demonstration project established in the Department of Agriculture (67 Fed. Reg. 70776 (2002)), shall become effective upon the date of enactment of this Act and shall remain in effect unless modified by law.

subsection.chapeau: In this title:

paragraph.heading: Specialty crop.—
paragraph.content: The term “specialty crop” has the meaning given the term in section 3 of the Specialty Crops Competitiveness Act of 2004 (7 U.S.C. 1621 note; Public Law 108–465).

paragraph.heading: State department of agriculture.—
paragraph.content: The term “State department of agriculture” means the agency, commission, or department of a State government responsible for protecting and promoting agriculture in the State.

section.heading: INDEPENDENT EVALUATION OF DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE COMMODITY PURCHASE PROCESS.

subsection.heading: Evaluation Required.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall arrange to have performed an independent evaluation of the purchasing processes (including the budgetary, statutory, and regulatory authority underlying the processes) used by the Department of Agriculture to implement the requirement that funds available under section 32 of the Act of August 24, 1935 (7 U.S.C. 612c), shall be principally devoted to perishable agricultural commodities.

subsection.heading: Submission of Results.—
subsection.content: Not later than 18 months after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Agriculture of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry of the Senate a report on the results of the evaluation.

subsection.heading: Initiative Authorized.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary may carry out a food safety education program to educate the public and persons in the fresh produce industry about—

paragraph.content: scientifically proven practices for reducing microbial pathogens on fresh produce; and
methods of reducing the threat of cross-contamination of fresh produce through sanitary handling practices.

subsection.heading: Cooperation.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may carry out the education program in cooperation with public and private partners.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out this section $1,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2008 through 2023, to remain available until expended.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall—

paragraph.content: carry out market news activities to provide timely price and shipment information of specialty crops in the United States; and
use funds made available under subsection (b) to increase the reporting levels for specialty crops in effect on the date of enactment of this Act.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: In addition to any other funds made available through annual appropriations for market news services, there is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $9,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2008 through 2023, to remain available until expended.

section.heading: EXPEDITED MARKETING ORDER FOR HASS AVOCADOS FOR GRADES AND STANDARDS AND OTHER PURPOSES.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall initiate procedures under the Agricultural Adjustment Act (7 U.S.C. 601 et seq.), reenacted with amendments by the Agricultural Marketing Agreement Act of 1937, to determine whether it would be appropriate to establish a Federal marketing order for Hass avocados relating to grades and standards and for other purposes under that Act.

paragraph.heading: Proposal for an order.—
paragraph.content: An organization of domestic avocado producers in existence on the date of enactment of this Act may request the issuance of, and submit to the Secretary a proposal for, an order described in subsection (a).

paragraph.heading: Publication of proposal.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 60 days after the date on which the Secretary receives a proposed order under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall initiate procedures described in subsection (a) to determine whether the proposed order should proceed.

subsection.heading: Effective Date.—
subsection.content: Any order issued under this section shall become effective not later than 15 months after the date on which the Secretary initiates procedures under the Agricultural Adjustment Act (7 U.S.C. 601 et seq.), reenacted with amendments by the Agricultural Marketing Agreement Act of 1937.

section.heading: REGULATIONS TO IMPROVE MANAGEMENT AND OVERSIGHT OF CERTAIN REGULATED ARTICLES.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 18 months after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall—

paragraph.content: take action on each issue identified in the document entitled “Lessons Learned and Revisions under Consideration for APHIS' Biotechnology Framework”, dated October 4, 2007; and
as the Secretary considers appropriate, promulgate regulations to improve the management and oversight of articles regulated under the Plant Protection Act (7 U.S.C. 7701 et seq.).

subsection.heading: Inclusions.—
subsection.chapeau: In carrying out subsection (a), the Secretary shall take actions that are designed to enhance—

paragraph.content: the quality and completeness of records;
the availability of representative samples;
the maintenance of identity and control in the event of an unauthorized release;
corrective actions in the event of an unauthorized release;
protocols for conducting molecular forensics;
clarity in contractual agreements;
the use of the latest scientific techniques for isolation and confinement distances;
standards for quality management systems and effective research; and
the design of electronic permits to store documents and other information relating to the permit and notification processes.

subsection.heading: Consideration.—
subsection.chapeau: In carrying out subsection (a), the Secretary shall consider—

paragraph.chapeau: establishing—

subparagraph.content: a system of risk-based categories to classify each regulated article;
a means to identify regulated articles (including the retention of seed samples); and
standards for isolation and containment distances; and

paragraph.chapeau: requiring permit holders—

subparagraph.content: to maintain a positive chain of custody;
to provide for the maintenance of records;
to provide for the accounting of material;
to conduct periodic audits;
to establish an appropriate training program;
to provide contingency and corrective action plans; and
to submit reports as the Secretary considers to be appropriate.

section.heading: PEST AND DISEASE REVOLVING LOAN FUND.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The term “authorized equipment” means any equipment necessary for the management of forest land.

subparagraph.heading: Inclusions.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The term “authorized equipment” includes—

clause.content: cherry pickers;

subclause.content: the construction of staging and marshalling areas;
the planting of trees; and
the surveying of forest land;

clause.content: vehicles capable of transporting harvested trees;
wood chippers; and
any other appropriate equipment, as determined by the Secretary.

paragraph.heading: Fund.—
paragraph.content: The term “Fund” means the Pest and Disease Revolving Loan Fund established by subsection (b).

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of Agriculture, acting through the Deputy Chief of the State and Private Forestry organization.

subsection.heading: Establishment of Fund.—
subsection.content: There is established in the Treasury of the United States a revolving fund, to be known as the “Pest and Disease Revolving Loan Fund”, consisting of such amounts as are appropriated to the Fund under subsection (f).

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Subject to paragraph (2), on request by the Secretary, the Secretary of the Treasury shall transfer from the Fund to the Secretary such amounts as the Secretary determines are necessary to provide loans under subsection (e).

paragraph.heading: Administrative expenses.—
paragraph.content: An amount not exceeding 10 percent of the amounts in the Fund shall be available for each fiscal year to pay the administrative expenses necessary to carry out this section.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The amounts required to be transferred to the Fund under this section shall be transferred at least monthly from the general fund of the Treasury to the Fund on the basis of estimates made by the Secretary of the Treasury.

paragraph.heading: Adjustments.—
paragraph.content: Proper adjustment shall be made in amounts subsequently transferred to the extent prior estimates were in excess of or less than the amounts required to be transferred.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall use amounts in the Fund to provide loans to eligible units of local government to finance purchases of authorized equipment to monitor, remove, dispose of, and replace infested trees that are located—

clause.content: on land under the jurisdiction of the eligible units of local government; and
within the borders of quarantine areas infested by plant pests.

subparagraph.heading: Maximum amount.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The maximum amount of a loan that may be provided by the Secretary to an eligible unit of local government under this subsection shall be the lesser of—

clause.content: the amount that the eligible unit of local government has appropriated to finance purchases of authorized equipment in accordance with subparagraph (A); or

subparagraph.heading: Interest rate.—
subparagraph.content: The interest rate on any loan made by the Secretary under this paragraph shall be a rate equal to 2 percent.

subparagraph.heading: Report.—
subparagraph.content: Not later than 180 days after the date on which an eligible unit of local government receives a loan provided by the Secretary under subparagraph (A), the eligible unit of local government shall submit to the Secretary a report that describes each purchase made by the eligible unit of local government using assistance provided through the loan.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: To be eligible to receive a loan from the Secretary under paragraph (1), in accordance with each requirement described in subparagraph (B), an eligible unit of local government shall enter into an agreement with the Secretary to establish a loan repayment schedule relating to the repayment of the loan.

subparagraph.heading: Requirements relating to loan repayment schedule.—
subparagraph.chapeau: A loan repayment schedule established under subparagraph (A) shall require the eligible unit of local government—

clause.chapeau: to repay to the Secretary of the Treasury, not later than 1 year after the date on which the eligible unit of local government receives a loan under paragraph (1), and semiannually thereafter, an amount equal to the quotient obtained by dividing—

subclause.content: the principal amount of the loan (including interest); by
the total quantity of payments that the eligible unit of local government is required to make during the repayment period of the loan; and

clause.content: not later than 20 years after the date on which the eligible unit of local government receives a loan under paragraph (1), to complete repayment to the Secretary of the Treasury of the loan made under this section (including interest).

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There are authorized to be appropriated to the Fund such sums as are necessary to carry out this section.

section.heading: MARKET LOSS ASSISTANCE FOR ASPARAGUS PRODUCERS.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: As soon as practicable after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall make payments to producers of the 2007 crop of asparagus for market loss resulting from imports during the 2004 through 2007 crop years.

subsection.heading: Payment Rate.—
subsection.content: The payment rate for a payment under this section shall be based on the reduction in revenue received by asparagus producers associated with imports during the 2004 through 2007 crop years.

subsection.heading: Payment Quantity.—
subsection.content: The payment quantity for asparagus for which the producers on a farm are eligible for payments under this section shall be equal to the average quantity of the 2003 crop of asparagus produced by producers on the farm.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Subject to paragraph (2), the Secretary shall make available $15,000,000 of the funds of the Commodity Credit Corporation to carry out a program to provide market loss payments to producers of asparagus under this section.

paragraph.heading: Allocation.—
paragraph.chapeau: Of the amount made available under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall use—

subparagraph.content: $7,500,000 to make payments to producers of asparagus for the fresh market; and
$7,500,000 to make payments to producers of asparagus for the processed or frozen market.

paragraph.heading: Study.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall conduct a study on the effects of requiring packer processing plants to report to the Secretary information on wholesale pork cuts (including price and volume information), including—

subparagraph.content: the positive or negative economic effects on producers and consumers; and
the effects of a confidentiality requirement on mandatory reporting.

paragraph.heading: Information.—
paragraph.content: During the period preceding the submission of the report under paragraph (3), the Secretary may collect, and each packer processing plant shall provide, such information as is necessary to enable the Secretary to conduct the study required under paragraph (1).

paragraph.heading: Report.—
paragraph.content: Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Agriculture of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry of the Senate a report on the results of the study conducted under paragraph (1).

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There are authorized to be appropriated such sums as may be necessary to carry out this section.

subsection.chapeau: As soon as practicable, but not later than 2 years after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Agriculture shall promulgate regulations with respect to the Packers and Stockyards Act, 1921 (7 U.S.C. 181 et seq.) to establish criteria that the Secretary will consider in determining—

paragraph.content: whether an undue or unreasonable preference or advantage has occurred in violation of such Act;
whether a live poultry dealer has provided reasonable notice to poultry growers of any suspension of the delivery of birds under a poultry growing arrangement;
when a requirement of additional capital investments over the life of a poultry growing arrangement or swine production contract constitutes a violation of such Act; and

if a live poultry dealer or swine contractor has provided a reasonable period of time for a poultry grower or a swine production contract grower to remedy a breach of contract that could lead to termination of the poultry growing arrangement or swine production contract.

section.heading: SENSE OF CONGRESS REGARDING PSEUDORABIES ERADICATION PROGRAM.

subsection.chapeau: It is the sense of Congress that—

paragraph.content: the Secretary of Agriculture should recognize the threat feral swine pose to the domestic swine population and the entire livestock industry;
keeping the United States commercial swine herd free of pseudorabies is essential to maintaining and growing pork export markets;
the establishment and continued support of a swine surveillance system will assist the swine industry in the monitoring, surveillance, and eradication of pseudorabies; and
pseudorabies eradication is a high priority that the Secretary should carry out under the authorities of the Animal Health Protection Act.

section.heading: SENSE OF CONGRESS REGARDING THE CATTLE FEVER TICK ERADICATION PROGRAM.

subsection.chapeau: It is the sense of Congress that—

paragraph.content: the cattle fever tick and the southern cattle tick are vectors of the causal agent of babesiosis, a severe and often fatal disease of cattle; and

paragraph.chapeau: implementing a national strategic plan for the cattle fever tick eradication program is a high priority that the Secretary of Agriculture should carry out in order to—

subparagraph.content: prevent the entry of cattle fever ticks into the United States;
enhance and maintain an effective surveillance program to rapidly detect any cattle fever tick incursions; and
research, identify, and procure the tools and knowledge necessary to prevent and eradicate cattle fever ticks in the United States.

paragraph.heading: Establishment.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Agriculture shall establish a voluntary trichinae certification program. Such program shall include the facilitation of the export of pork products and certification services related to such products.

paragraph.heading: Regulations.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall issue final regulations to implement the program under paragraph (1) not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act.

paragraph.heading: Report.—
paragraph.chapeau: If final regulations are not published in accordance with paragraph (2) within 90 days of the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Agriculture of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry of the Senate a report containing—

subparagraph.content: an explanation of why the final regulations have not been issued in accordance with paragraph (2); and
the date on which the Secretary expects to issue such final regulations.

subsection.heading: Funding.—
subsection.content: Subject to the availability of appropriations under subsection (d)(1)(A) of section 10405 of the Animal Health Protection Act (7 U.S.C. 8304), as added by subsection (c), the Secretary shall use not less than $6,200,000 of the funds made available under such subsection to carry out subsection (a).

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary of Agriculture may enter into a cooperative agreement with an eligible entity to carry out a project under a national aquatic animal health plan under the authority of the Secretary under section 10411 of the Animal Health Protection Act (7 U.S.C. 8310) for the purpose of detecting, controlling, or eradicating diseases of aquaculture species and promoting species-specific best management practices.

subsection.heading: Cooperative Agreements Between Eligible Entities and the Secretary.—

paragraph.heading: Duties.—
paragraph.chapeau: As a condition of entering into a cooperative agreement with the Secretary under this section, an eligible entity shall agree to—

subparagraph.content: assume responsibility for the non-Federal share of the cost of carrying out the project under the national aquatic health plan, as determined by the Secretary in accordance with paragraph (2); and
act in accordance with applicable disease and species specific best management practices relating to activities to be carried out under such project.

paragraph.heading: Non-federal share.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall determine the non-Federal share of the cost of carrying out a project under the national aquatic health plan on a case-by-case basis for each such project. Such non-Federal share may be provided in cash or in-kind.

subsection.heading: Applicability of Other Laws.—
subsection.content: In carrying out this section, the Secretary may make use of the authorities under the Animal Health Protection Act (7 U.S.C. 8301 et seq.), including the authority to carry out operations and measures to detect, control, and eradicate pests and diseases and the authority to pay claims arising out of the destruction of any animal, article, or means of conveyance.

subsection.heading: Eligible Entity Defined.—
subsection.content: In this section, the term “eligible entity” means a State, a political subdivision of a State, Indian tribe, or other appropriate entity, as determined by the Secretary of Agriculture.

subsection.heading: Study.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary of Agriculture shall conduct a study to evaluate the role of animal manure as a source of fertilizer and its potential additional uses. Such study shall include—

paragraph.content: a determination of the extent to which animal manure is utilized as fertilizer in agricultural operations by type (including species and agronomic practices employed) and size;
an evaluation of the potential impact on consumers and on agricultural operations (by size) resulting from limitations being placed on the utilization of animal manure as fertilizer; and

an evaluation of the effects on agriculture production contributable to the increased competition for animal manure use due to bioenergy production, including as a feedstock or a replacement for fossil fuels.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.content: Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Agriculture of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry of the Senate the results of the study conducted under subsection (a).

subtitle.heading: Socially Disadvantaged Producers and Limited Resource Producers

section.heading: OVERSIGHT AND COMPLIANCE.
section.content: The Secretary, acting through the Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights of the Department of Agriculture, shall use the reports described in subsection (c) of section 2501A of the Food, Agriculture, Conservation, and Trade Act of 1990 (7 U.S.C. 2279–1), as amended by section 14006, in the conduct of oversight and evaluation of civil rights compliance.

subsection.heading: Establishment.—
subsection.content: Not later than 18 months after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Agriculture shall establish an advisory committee, to be known as the “Advisory Committee on Minority Farmers” (in this section referred to as the “Committee”).

subsection.heading: Duties.—
subsection.chapeau: The Committee shall provide advice to the Secretary on—

paragraph.content: the implementation of section 2501 of the Food, Agriculture, Conservation, and Trade Act of 1990 (7 U.S.C. 2279);
methods of maximizing the participation of minority farmers and ranchers in Department of Agriculture programs; and
civil rights activities within the Department as such activities relate to participants in such programs.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Committee shall be composed of not more than 15 members, who shall be appointed by the Secretary, and shall include—

subparagraph.content: not less than four socially disadvantaged farmers or ranchers (as defined in section 2501(e)(2) of the Food, Agriculture, Conservation, and Trade Act of 1990 (7 U.S.C. 2279(e)(2)));
not less than two representatives of nonprofit organizations with a history of working with minority farmers and ranchers;
not less than two civil rights professionals;
not less than two representatives of institutions of higher education with demonstrated experience working with minority farmers and ranchers; and
such other persons as the Secretary considers appropriate.

paragraph.heading: Ex-officio members.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary may appoint such employees of the Department of Agriculture as the Secretary considers appropriate to serve as ex-officio members of the Committee.

section.heading: REPORT OF CIVIL RIGHTS COMPLAINTS, RESOLUTIONS, AND ACTIONS.

subsection.chapeau: Each year, the Secretary shall—

paragraph.chapeau: prepare a report that describes, for each agency of the Department of Agriculture—

subparagraph.content: the number of civil rights complaints filed that relate to the agency, including whether a complaint is a program complaint or an employment complaint;
the length of time the agency took to process each civil rights complaint;
the number of proceedings brought against the agency, including the number of complaints described in paragraph (1) that were resolved with a finding of discrimination; and
the number and type of personnel actions taken by the agency following resolution of civil rights complaints;

paragraph.content: submit to the Committee on Agriculture of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry of the Senate a copy of the report; and
make the report available to the public by posting the report on the website of the Department.

section.heading: SENSE OF CONGRESS RELATING TO CLAIMS BROUGHT BY SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED FARMERS OR RANCHERS.
section.content: It is the sense of Congress that all pending claims and class actions brought against the Department of Agriculture by socially disadvantaged farmers or ranchers (as defined in section 355(e) of the Consolidated Farm and Rural Development Act (7 U.S.C. 2003(e)), including Native American, Hispanic, and female farmers or ranchers, based on racial, ethnic, or gender discrimination in farm program participation should be resolved in an expeditious and just manner.

section.heading: DETERMINATION ON MERITS OF PIGFORD CLAIMS.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Consent decree.—
paragraph.content: The term “consent decree” means the consent decree in the case of Pigford v. Glickman, approved by the United States District Court for the District of Columbia on April 14, 1999.

paragraph.heading: Department.—
paragraph.content: The term “Department” means the Department of Agriculture.

paragraph.heading: Pigford claim.—
paragraph.content: The term “Pigford claim” means a discrimination complaint, as defined by section 1(h) of the consent decree and documented under section 5(b) of the consent decree.

paragraph.heading: Pigford claimant.—
paragraph.content: The term “Pigford claimant” means an individual who previously submitted a late-filing request under section 5(g) of the consent decree.

subsection.heading: Determination on Merits.—
subsection.content: Any Pigford claimant who has not previously obtained a determination on the merits of a Pigford claim may, in a civil action brought in the United States District Court for the District of Columbia, obtain that determination.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Subject to paragraph (2), all payments or debt relief (including any limitation on foreclosure under subsection (h)) shall be made exclusively from funds made available under subsection (i).

paragraph.heading: Maximum amount.—
paragraph.content: The total amount of payments and debt relief pursuant to actions commenced under subsection (b) shall not exceed $100,000,000.

subsection.heading: Intent of Congress as to Remedial Nature of Section.—
subsection.content: It is the intent of Congress that this section be liberally construed so as to effectuate its remedial purpose of giving a full determination on the merits for each Pigford claim previously denied that determination.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Not later than 120 days after the Secretary receives notice of a complaint filed by a claimant under subsection (b), the Secretary shall provide to the claimant a report on farm credit loans and noncredit benefits, as appropriate, made within the claimant's county (or if no documents are found, within an adjacent county as determined by the claimant), by the Department during the period beginning on January 1 of the year preceding the period covered by the complaint and ending on December 31 of the year following the period.

subparagraph.heading: Requirements.—
subparagraph.chapeau: A report under subparagraph (A) shall contain information on all persons whose application for a loan or benefit was accepted, including—

clause.content: the race of the applicant;
the date of application;
the date of the loan or benefit decision, as appropriate;
the location of the office making the loan or benefit decision, as appropriate;
all data relevant to the decisionmaking process for the loan or benefit, as appropriate; and
all data relevant to the servicing of the loan or benefit, as appropriate.

paragraph.heading: No personally identifiable information.—
paragraph.content: The reports provided pursuant to paragraph (1) shall not contain any information that would identify any person who applied for a loan from the Department.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall—

clause.content: provide to claimants the reports required under paragraph (1) as quickly as practicable after the Secretary receives notice of a complaint filed by a claimant under subsection (b); and
devote such resources of the Department as are necessary to make providing the reports expeditiously a high priority of the Department.

subparagraph.heading: Extension.—
subparagraph.content: A court may extend the deadline for providing the report required in a particular case under paragraph (1) if the Secretary establishes that meeting the deadline is not feasible and demonstrates a continuing effort and commitment to provide the required report expeditiously.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: Any person filing a complaint under this section for discrimination in the application for, or making or servicing of, a farm loan, at the discretion of the person, may seek liquidated damages of $50,000, discharge of the debt that was incurred under, or affected by, the 1 or more programs that were the subject of the 1 or more discrimination claims that are the subject of the person's complaint, and a tax payment in the amount equal to 25 percent of the liquidated damages and loan principal discharged, in which case—

subparagraph.content: if only such damages, debt discharge, and tax payment are sought, the complainant shall be able to prove the case of the complainant by substantial evidence (as defined in section 1(l) of the consent decree); and
the court shall decide the case based on a review of documents submitted by the complainant and defendant relevant to the issues of liability and damages.

subparagraph.heading: Standard.—
subparagraph.content: In any case in which a claimant asserts a noncredit claim under a benefit program of the Department, the court shall determine the merits of the claim in accordance with section 9(b)(i) of the consent decree.

subparagraph.heading: Relief.—
subparagraph.content: A claimant who prevails on a claim of discrimination involving a noncredit benefit program of the Department shall be entitled to a payment by the Department in a total amount of $3,000, without regard to the number of such claims on which the claimant prevails.

subsection.heading: Actual Damages.—
subsection.content: A claimant who files a claim under this section for discrimination under subsection (b) but not under subsection (f) and who prevails on the claim shall be entitled to actual damages sustained by the claimant.

subsection.heading: Limitation on Foreclosures.—
subsection.chapeau: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, during the pendency of a Pigford claim, the Secretary may not begin acceleration on or foreclosure of a loan if—

paragraph.content: the borrower is a Pigford claimant; and
makes a prima facie case in an appropriate administrative proceeding that the acceleration or foreclosure is related to a Pigford claim.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Of the funds of the Commodity Credit Corporation, the Secretary shall make available for payments and debt relief in satisfaction of claims against the United States under subsection (b) and for any actions under subsection (g) $100,000,000 for fiscal year 2008, to remain available until expended.

paragraph.heading: Authorization of appropriations.—
paragraph.content: In addition to funds made available under paragraph (1), there are authorized to be appropriated such sums as are necessary to carry out this section.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act and every 180 days thereafter until the funds made available under subsection (i) are depleted, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on the Judiciary of the House of Representatives and the Committee on the Judiciary of the Senate a report that describes the status of available funds under subsection (i) and the number of pending claims under subsection (f).

paragraph.heading: Depletion of funds report.—
paragraph.content: In addition to the reports required under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on the Judiciary of the House of Representatives and the Committee on the Judiciary of the Senate a report that notifies the Committees when 75 percent of the funds made available under subsection (i)(1) have been depleted.

subsection.heading: Termination of Authority.—
subsection.content: The authority to file a claim under this section terminates 2 years after the date of the enactment of this Act.

section.heading: SHORT TITLE.
section.content: This subtitle may be cited as the “Agricultural Security Improvement Act of 2008”.

subsection.chapeau: In this subtitle:

paragraph.heading: Agent.—
paragraph.content: The term “agent” means a nuclear, biological, chemical, or radiological substance that causes agricultural disease or the adulteration of products regulated by the Secretary of Agriculture under any provision of law.

paragraph.heading: Agricultural biosecurity.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “agricultural biosecurity” means protection from an agent that poses a threat to—

subparagraph.content: plant or animal health;
public health as it relates to the adulteration of products regulated by the Secretary of Agriculture under any provision of law that is caused by exposure to an agent; or
the environment as it relates to agriculture facilities, farmland, and air and water within the immediate vicinity of an area associated with an agricultural disease or outbreak.

paragraph.heading: Agricultural countermeasure.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “agricultural countermeasure”—

subparagraph.content: means a product, practice, or technology that is intended to enhance or maintain the agricultural biosecurity of the United States; and
does not include a product, practice, or technology used solely in response to a human medical incident or public health emergency not related to agriculture.

paragraph.heading: Agricultural disease.—
paragraph.content: The term “agricultural disease” has the meaning given the term by the Secretary.

paragraph.heading: Agricultural disease emergency.—
paragraph.content: The term “agricultural disease emergency” means an incident of agricultural disease that requires prompt action to prevent significant damage to people, plants, or animals.

paragraph.heading: Agroterrorist act.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “agroterrorist act” means an act that—

subparagraph.chapeau: causes or attempts to cause—

clause.content: damage to agriculture; or
injury to a person associated with agriculture; and

subparagraph.chapeau: is committed or appears to be committed with the intent to—

clause.content: intimidate or coerce a civilian population; or
disrupt the agricultural industry in order to influence the policy of a government by intimidation or coercion.

paragraph.heading: Animal.—
paragraph.content: The term “animal” has the meaning given the term in section 10403 of the Animal Health Protection Act of 2002 (7 U.S.C. 8302).

paragraph.heading: Department.—
paragraph.content: The term “Department” means the Department of Agriculture.

paragraph.heading: Development.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “development” means—

subparagraph.content: research leading to the identification of products or technologies intended for use as agricultural countermeasures to protect animal health;
the formulation, production, and subsequent modification of those products or technologies;
the conduct of in vitro and in vivo studies;
the conduct of field, efficacy, and safety studies;
the preparation of an application for marketing approval for submission to an applicable agency; or
other actions taken by an applicable agency in a case in which an agricultural countermeasure is procured or used prior to issuance of a license or other form of Federal Government approval.

paragraph.heading: Plant.—
paragraph.content: The term “plant” has the meaning given the term in section 411 of the Plant Protection Act of 2000 (7 U.S.C. 7702).

paragraph.heading: Qualified agricultural countermeasure.—
paragraph.content: The term “qualified agricultural countermeasure” means an agricultural countermeasure that the Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of Homeland Security, determines to be a priority in order to address an agricultural biosecurity threat.

chapter.heading: AGRICULTURAL SECURITY
chapter.editorialNote: [Section 14111 was repealed by section 122201 of Public Law 115–334.]

subsection.heading: Establishment.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall establish a communication center within the Department to—

paragraph.content: collect and disseminate information and prepare for an agricultural disease emergency, agroterrorist act, or other threat to agricultural biosecurity; and
coordinate activities described in paragraph (1) among agencies and offices within the Department.

subsection.heading: Relation to Existing DHS Communication Systems.—

paragraph.heading: Consistency and coordination.—
paragraph.content: The communication center established under subsection (a) shall, to the maximum extent practicable, share and coordinate the dissemination of timely information with the Department of Homeland Security and other communication systems of appropriate Federal departments and agencies.

paragraph.heading: Avoiding redundancies.—
paragraph.content: Paragraph (1) shall not be construed to impede, conflict with, or duplicate the communications activities performed by the Secretary of Homeland Security under any provision of law.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.chapeau: There are authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section—

paragraph.content: such sums as are necessary for each of fiscal years 2008 through 2013; and
$2,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2014 through 2023.

section.heading: ASSISTANCE TO BUILD LOCAL CAPACITY IN AGRICULTURAL BIOSECURITY PLANNING, PREPAREDNESS, AND RESPONSE.

paragraph.heading: Grant assistance.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall establish a competitive grant program to support the development and expansion of advanced training programs in agricultural biosecurity planning and response for food science professionals and veterinarians.

paragraph.heading: Authorization of appropriations.—
paragraph.chapeau: There are authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out this subsection—

subparagraph.content: such sums as are necessary for each of fiscal years 2008 through 2013; and
$15,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2014 through 2023.

paragraph.heading: Grant and loan assistance.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall establish a competitive grant and low-interest loan assistance program to assist States in assessing agricultural disease response capability.

paragraph.heading: Authorization of appropriations.—
paragraph.chapeau: There are authorized to be appropriated to carry out this subsection—

subparagraph.content: $25,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2008 through 2013; and
$15,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2014 through 2023.

section.heading: RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT OF AGRICULTURAL COUNTERMEASURES.

paragraph.heading: Competitive grant program.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall establish a competitive grant program to encourage basic and applied research and the development of qualified agricultural countermeasures.

paragraph.heading: Waiver in emergencies.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary may waive the requirement under paragraph (1) that a grant be provided on a competitive basis if—

subparagraph.content: the Secretary has declared a plant or animal disease emergency under the Plant Protection Act (7 U.S.C. 7701 et seq.) or the Animal Health Protection Act (7 U.S.C. 8301 et seq.); and
waiving the requirement would lead to the rapid development of a qualified agricultural countermeasure, as determined by the Secretary.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.chapeau: There are authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section—

paragraph.content: $50,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2008 through 2013; and
$15,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2014 through 2023.

subsection.heading: Competitive Grant Program.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall establish a competitive grant program to promote the development of teaching programs in agriculture, veterinary medicine, and disciplines closely allied to the food and agriculture system to increase the number of trained individuals with an expertise in agricultural biosecurity.

subsection.heading: Eligibility.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary may award a grant under this section only to an entity that is—

paragraph.content: an accredited school of veterinary medicine; or

paragraph.chapeau: a department of an institution of higher education with a primary focus on—

subparagraph.content: comparative medicine;
veterinary science; or
agricultural biosecurity.

subsection.heading: Preference.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall give preference in awarding grants based on the ability of an applicant—

paragraph.content: to increase the number of veterinarians or individuals with advanced degrees in food and agriculture disciplines who are trained in agricultural biosecurity practice areas;
to increase research capacity in areas of agricultural biosecurity; or
to fill critical agricultural biosecurity shortage situations outside of the Federal Government.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: Amounts received under this section shall be used by a grantee to pay—

subparagraph.content: costs associated with the acquisition of equipment and other capital costs relating to the expansion of food, agriculture, and veterinary medicine teaching programs in agricultural biosecurity;

capital costs associated with the expansion of academic programs that offer postgraduate training for veterinarians or concurrent training for veterinary students in specific areas of specialization; or
other capacity and infrastructure program costs that the Secretary considers appropriate.

paragraph.heading: Limitation.—
paragraph.content: Funds received under this section may not be used for the construction, renovation, or rehabilitation of a building or facility.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.chapeau: There are authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section—

paragraph.content: such sums as are necessary for each of fiscal years 2008 through 2013, to remain available until expended; and
$5,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2014 through 2023, to remain available until expended.

section.heading: GRANTS TO REDUCE PRODUCTION OF METHAMPHETAMINES FROM ANHYDROUS AMMONIA.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: Eligible entity.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “eligible entity” means—

subparagraph.content: a producer of agricultural commodities;
a cooperative association, a majority of the members of which produce or process agricultural commodities; or

subparagraph.chapeau: a person in the trade or business of—

clause.content: selling an agricultural product (including an agricultural chemical) at retail, predominantly to farmers and ranchers; or
aerial and ground application of an agricultural chemical.

paragraph.heading: Nurse tank.—
